plain: Too ready to believe things without proof.

webster.text: Apt to believe without sufficient evidence; unsuspecting; easily deceived.

example.quote: But notwithstanding the strongest assertions that there are no wolves in our country, if we see their footsteps in every public path, we should be very credulous and unwise to trust our flocks abroad, and to believe that those who advised us to do it were very anxious for their preservation.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, July 2, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
